verdicts.title: Non-Additive Discrepancy: Coverage Functions in a Beck-Fiala Setting
verdicts.abstract_excerpt:
Recent concurrent work by Dupré la Tour and Fujii and by Hollender, Manurangsi, Meka, and Suksompong [ITCS'26] introduced a generalization of classical discrepancy theory to non-additive functions, motivated by applications in fair division. As many classical techniques from discrepancy theory seem to fail in this setting, including linear algebraic methods like the Beck-Fiala Theorem [Discrete Appl. Math '81], it remains widely open whether comparable non-additive bounds can be achieved.
  Towa
verdicts.judge_reasoning: The abstract concerns non-additive discrepancy bounds for coverage functions in a Beck-Fiala-like sparse setting ('we prove a constructive discrepancy bound that is polynomial in t, k, and log n'), with no mention of DPLL search trees, tree-resolution, or 3-CNF proof complexity, so it neither supports nor refutes the specific clause-variable conjecture.

verdicts.title: An Improved Bound for the Beck-Fiala Conjecture
verdicts.abstract_excerpt: In 1981, Beck and Fiala [Discrete Appl. Math, 1981] conjectured that given a set system $A \in \{0,1\}^{m \times n}$ with degree at most $k$ (i.e., each column of $A$ has at most $k$ non-zeros), its combinatorial discrepancy $\mathsf{disc}(A) := \min_{x \in \{\pm 1\}^n} \|Ax\|_\infty$ is at most $O(\sqrt{k})$. Previously, the best-known bounds for this conjecture were either $O(k)$, first established by Beck and Fiala [Discrete Appl. Math, 1981], or $O(\sqrt{k \log n})$, first proved by Banaszcz
verdicts.judge_reasoning: The abstract concerns asymptotic discrepancy upper bounds O(sqrt(k log log n)) for the Beck-Fiala conjecture on general degree-k set systems, not a connection between Beck-Fiala slack of clause-variable hypergraphs and DPLL tree-resolution leaf counts on small unsatisfiable 3-CNFs.

verdicts.title: An improvement of the Beck-Fiala theorem
verdicts.abstract_excerpt: In 1981 Beck and Fiala proved an upper bound for the discrepancy of a set system of degree d that is independent of the size of the ground set. In the intervening years the bound has been decreased from 2d-2 to 2d-4. We improve the bound to 2d-log* d.
verdicts.judge_reasoning: The abstract only improves the classical Beck-Fiala discrepancy bound from 2d-4 to 2d-log*d; it says nothing about DPLL/tree-resolution leaf counts or clause-variable hypergraphs of 3-CNFs, so it neither supports nor refutes the specific inequality log2(L_DPLL(F)) >= delta(F)/3 - 1.
